projectTitle: A DNA-based recorder of transient fermentation stress in Pichia pastoris
tagline: Turn fleeting glucose and oxygen limitation during a fermentation run into permanent, readable marks in DNA.
summary: Jilin-China built a two-channel genetic event recorder: pGTH1 drives Cre (recording glucose limitation) acting on a lox71/lox66 pair, and PsADH2 drives FLP (recording oxygen limitation) acting on an FRT-LE/FRT-RE pair, each inversion flipping a fluorescent reporter read after the run. Five separate models answer five design questions that experiments could not settle: which synonymous FLP sequence to synthesise, how bulk glucose maps to a promoter input, whether an alginate capsule isolates its cells from the broth, what DNA states the construct can occupy, and which published promoter evidence actually applies. The most striking feature is epistemic discipline: nearly every claim is accompanied by a statement of what the calculation does NOT establish, and when the glucose model's predicted low-glucose crossing time (7.56 h) disagreed with the measured 0.11 g/L at 8 h, the team reported the disagreement and downgraded the 0.05 g/L figure to a scenario threshold rather than a promoter activation threshold.

dry.frameworks: Five models, each tied to a design action. (1) RecombiOpt — synonymous CDS design. It works in the real construct context (the 6,628 nt pET28a-FLP plasmid with a BL21(DE3) host profile), correctly identifies that translation starts at position 107 while FLP starts at 221 because of a 114 nt / 38 aa fusion tag, and computes accessibility as an opening free energy Delta_G_open = -RT ln P_unpaired for the contiguous 48 nt window [-24, +24) around the ACTUAL translation start using local RNA folding in ViennaRNA at 30 C with W = L = 210 nt. A greedy coordinate-descent local search over the first 10/15/30 FLP codons (max three rounds, methionine preserved) produced 'target5prime-30', which changed only 15 nt across 14 codons and cut opening energy from 10.6473 to 7.9007 kcal/mol while leaving CAI essentially flat (0.5184 to 0.5246), versus a constrained-maxCAI design that changed 352 nt to reach CAI 0.9948 but only reached 8.3520 kcal/mol. A complementary RNAstructure 6.6 analysis at 30 C compared MFE and mean single-base unpaired probability across the first 30, 90, 150 nt and full 1,272 nt CDS windows. (2) Glucose model — a coupled ODE of enzymatic glucose release, cellular uptake and OD growth. Sterile release was calibrated FIRST and separately in water and in YP medium (no parameter transfer between them) as a sum of first-order releasable pools dD_i/dt = -k_i D_i with r_h(t) = sum k_i D_i, giving the closed form G(t) = G_0 + sum A_i(1 - exp(-k_i t)); a one-pool model was retained unless adding a second pool cut fitting RMSE by more than 40%. Uptake and growth were then fitted jointly with shared parameters across conditions, with time and condition holdouts. (3) Capsule2Memory — a spherically symmetric reaction-diffusion PDE for an immobilisation bead, dG/dt = (D_eff/r^2) d/dr(r^2 dG/dr) - X q_max G/(K_m + G) with Monod uptake, solved under three distinct boundary regimes (prescribed surface concentration; a Robin condition D_eff dG/dr|_R = k_L[G_b - G(R,t)] for finite interfacial transfer; and a finite-bath case with instantaneous partitioning c_g(R,t) = K C_b(t) that solves bath and interior together including the sampling withdrawals). Four model variants are compared — M0 (follows input directly), M1 (diffusion only), M2 (diffusion plus uptake), M2-lumped (one uniform internal state with k_eff = 15 D_eff/R^2, where the factor 15 is derived from the steady-state mean deficit of a sphere with constant volumetric uptake) — and the page explicitly derives the exact volume-averaged balance and states why the lumped closure is an approximation, since Monod uptake is nonlinear so <G/(K_m+G)>_V is not G_bar/(K_m+G_bar). Numerics are a spherical-shell finite-volume discretisation with implicit BDF integration, solved separately across input discontinuities. (4) Recombistate — a discrete state machine over DNA sequences. The 16,098 bp final plasmid is annotated down to coordinates (lox71 at 4,767-4,800, lox66 at 6,050-6,083, FRT-LE at 6,272-6,305, FRT-RE at 7,784-7,817, with the reverse-strand FRT-RE reported in both genomic-forward and feature-oriented conventions), and the state graph is enumerated on an earlier 3,367 bp reporter fragment under specified Cre/lox and FLP/FRT rules, max two recombination steps, yielding four distinct DNA sequences, four transitions and five event histories. The key result is a negative one about observability: the two orderings of events A and B converge on the SAME final sequence, so the final DNA does not retain event order. (5) FermentPromoterBank — a promoter evidence registry (9 core constructs, 8 watchlist candidates, 252 discovery entries, 12 design entries) that keeps sequence boundaries, host and culture conditions in one record, explicitly described as not an activity predictor.
dry.dataviz: Twenty-two numbered figures, and the captions are the most instructive part of them. Each caption states the axis meaning, the exact computational settings used, and what the figure may not be read as: 'connecting lines guide the eye and do not represent a time course'; 'the panels use different metrics and horizontal scales'; 'Error bars and asterisks are reproduced from the original figure. Replicate counts, the error measure and the statistical comparisons are unspecified, so we do not infer P values or statistical significance from these marks'; 'the graph is a structural calculation under the registered FRT rule; it is not a measurement of four fluorescence channels'. Figure 3 plots mean paired gains with 95% intervals from 5,000 group-bootstrap resamples, and the caption notes the intervals come from saved out-of-fold predictions and do not include full-retraining uncertainty. Figure 1 is a model-dependency diagram that distinguishes solid arrows (within-module workflows and documented design selections) from dashed arrows (conceptual interfaces that are NOT a validated coupled prediction) — a distinction almost no iGEM team draws. Figure 4 shows the three-way trade-off (CAI, opening energy, nucleotide edits) as separate aligned panels rather than a composite score. Figure 20 is a conditional DNA-state graph that visually separates sequence states from event histories, making the two converging paths to S_CF legible.
dry.datascience: The machine-learning work is a model of restraint. They tested whether RNA structure features add information to expression proxy models by holding the ExtraTrees algorithm, base features and data splits fixed and only adding opening energy and local MFE, across three tasks (Boel expression levels, TIsigner detectable-expression labels, Nieuwkoop mRFP synonymous variants) with grouped five-fold validation and five random seeds — grouping by protein family for the first two and by experimental plate for the third, specifically to stop related samples appearing in both train and test. Gains were small but consistent: Boel QWK 0.1391 to 0.1677 (+0.0286 [0.0229, 0.0344]), TIsigner AP 0.8851 to 0.8997 (+0.0146), Nieuwkoop Spearman 0.7622 to 0.7906 (+0.0283), all five seeds positive — and they then note that even with RNA features the Boel QWK of ~0.168 means expression-level agreement 'remained limited', and that Boel and TIsigner share 2,363 protein-family components so positive results in both are not two independent replications. Crucially, they then DECLINED to use those models to rank their FLP candidates: an out-of-distribution protocol (MMseqs2 10-6d92c family search with predefined thresholds fident >= 0.30 and bidirectional coverage qcov, tcov >= 0.80, plus explicit feature distance, prediction disagreement and construct context) classified all 12 candidate-task combinations as OOD, so candidate selection was made on hard constraints (protein and vector invariance) plus a qualitative trade-off, with the team stating 'we did not add numerical weights after the fact' and that target5prime-30 'is not the unique optimum across every metric and window' since a five-window sensitivity analysis changed the ranking. Model selection followed predefined performance-and-complexity rules that retained simple linear models for two tasks and rejected frozen CodonBERT representations for lack of consistent gain. Wet-lab closure: FLP-Var (target5prime-30) gave a stronger anti-His Western signal than FLP-WT after 0.5 mM IPTG for 6 h and a higher OD600-normalised RFP recombination-reporter curve — reported as qualitative support only, with the team noting the two assays use different regulatory constructs, that OD600 normalisation does not equalise FLP amounts, and that no RNA-decay assay was run so the proposed hydrolysis-resistance mechanism remains a hypothesis. The glucose dataset is 138 concentration and OD600 records; six '<0.02 g/L' readings were retained as upper bounds rather than coerced to 0.02.
dry.software: RecombiOpt is a released tool (v0.3.0 noted) with host profiles for E. coli BL21(DE3) and P. pastoris GS115, a conditional synonymous generator, a separate 'engineering repair' step that searches for synonymous fixes to declared rule violations and then re-runs all checks, protein and vector invariant verification, and retained tool versions and complete parameters alongside every analysis. The team is explicit that a current optimize run cannot reproduce the entire historical study, and that repair 'addresses whether a sequence meets engineering requirements; it does not predict expression'. The validation table lists, per module, exactly which checks were completed and what evidence supports them — analytical and numerical checks plus replay of a public transport subcase for Capsule2Memory, comparison against an independent solver for the bacterial parameter example, mass-balance and numerical-refinement checks for the tracer experiment, grouped internal validation and OOD checks for RecombiOpt, sterile-source calibration plus joint fitting plus time and condition holdouts for the glucose model, and DNA/junction/convergence checks for Recombistate.
techniques: synonymous codon design with greedy coordinate descent
RNA local folding accessibility / opening free energy
RNA secondary-structure MFE and base-pair probability analysis
codon adaptation index with project-specific host reference
supervised regression and classification with grouped cross-validation
out-of-distribution applicability protocol with prespecified thresholds
coupled ODE fitting with shared parameters across conditions
parsimony criterion for adding model components (40% RMSE rule)
spherically symmetric reaction-diffusion PDE with Monod kinetics
Dirichlet, Robin and finite-bath boundary conditions compared
volume averaging and lumped-parameter model reduction with derived closure

good.publicEngagement: A sustained programme rather than one-off events, organised under the 'Continue' step of their 5C Guidelines: the 5th Annual Community Day, the Apricot Blossom Festival, high-school and middle-school outreach, a Popular Science Series Course, a Summer Science Exploration Camp, senior-community outreach and a Sci-Tech Festival, reaching audiences across generations and educational backgrounds through lectures, hands-on activity and conversation. A promotion brochure is published as a downloadable PDF.
good.ihp: The team built a named framework from the sociology-of-technology literature: a Social Shaping Loop of Encounter, Reflect, Respond, Rewrite, grounded in Argyris's distinction between single-loop learning (improving the existing method) and double-loop learning (questioning the assumptions behind it), layered on their own 5C Guidelines (Collect, Comprehend, Compromise, Continue) carried over from 2025, and framed by MacKenzie and Wajcman's The Social Shaping of Technology. They then applied the distinction honestly: single-loop work was adjusting recombinant expression conditions, codon optimisation, leakage-test conditions and hydrogel diffusion; the double loop was realising that a strong fluorescence signal does not establish industrial usefulness, and that the real questions are whether a recorded state accurately represents a relevant environmental event, whether the information stays interpretable after the event has passed, and whether the system works under representative fermentation conditions. Industrial engagement at BYHEALTH and vaccine and pharmaceutical production facilities surfaced stability, process compatibility, data interpretation and operational safety as criteria. Scientific exchange at the iGEM Northeast China Exchange and university visits fed directly into a modelling result: the Recombistate finding that different event sequences converge on the same final DNA state changed the design goal, pushing them toward a modular sensing-memory-readout toolkit while stating plainly that the toolkit is a direction rather than a validated set.
good.realWorld: The application target is industrial fermentation monitoring: a recorder that preserves information about transient stress events (glucose limitation, oxygen limitation) that a bulk probe reading cannot capture, read out after the run. Alginate-style encapsulation is part of the deployment concept, which is exactly why Capsule2Memory exists — the model shows that splitting one large bead into several of equal total biomass shortens the diffusion distance, but that insufficient interfacial exchange can still produce substantial error during a long low-glucose event, so size, cell loading and exchange capacity must be screened together rather than separately. The team repeatedly marks the boundary of the claim, noting that glucose trajectory, promoter response and DNA writing have not yet been measured in the same experiment.

images.caption: Figure 1: connections among the five models, with solid arrows for within-module workflows and documented design selections and dashed arrows for conceptual interfaces that are explicitly NOT a validated coupled prediction — a distinction that lets a reader see exactly where the chain of evidence is real and where it is aspiration.

Figure 4: the three-way trade-off between codon adaptation index, predicted RNA opening energy of the 48 nt translation-initiation region, and number of nucleotide edits, shown as three aligned panels. The locally optimised candidate changed 15 nt and reached the lowest opening energy (7.90 kcal/mol); the full-length maxCAI design changed 352 nt to reach CAI 0.9948 but only 8.35 kcal/mol.

Figure 12: dynamic responses to low-glucose events under equal-resource encapsulation designs, from the spherically symmetric reaction-diffusion model with Monod uptake. Splitting one bead into several of the same total biomass shortens the diffusion path, but finite interfacial exchange can still mistime a long low-glucose event.

Figure 20: the conditional DNA-state graph for the reporter fragment, which separates sequence states (S0, SC, SF, SCF) from event histories. The two paths into SCF are different orders of the same two events reaching an identical final sequence, so the recorder cannot report event order — a negative result that changed the design goal.

gemsTakeaway: Write every figure caption and every model claim with an explicit scope limit attached — what this calculation does not establish, which constructs and conditions it covers, which arrows in your diagram are validated and which are aspirational — and when a prediction disagrees with a measurement, publish the disagreement and demote the prediction rather than quietly dropping it. Jilin also shows the right way to use an off-the-shelf ML model: run a prespecified out-of-distribution check first, and if your target fails it, do not use the score.
